stories.title: Prosper and Versluys Close $50M Land Deal for $650M Miami Condo Tower
stories.excerpt: Prosper Group and Versluys Group have paid $50 million for a development site in Miami’s Brickell district, where they plan to build a $650 million condo tower, the joint venture announced. The 1-acre assemblage includes three parcels: one along the Miami River, with more than 300 feet of water frontage, as well as two adjacent inland spots at 66 Southwest Sixth Street and 625 Southwest First Avenue, near the Brickell City Center mixed-use complex. The joint venture plans to develop a 60-story waterfront high-rise with 181 condos. Vaster provided a $30.5 million loan for the acquisition, which has been under contract for at least eight months. The sellers, developers Two Roads Development and Newgard Development Group, are currently building another luxury complex on a neighboring lot at 99 Southwest Seventh Street. Last year, the joint venture nabbed a $513 million financing package for the construction of two condo towers: a 46-story, 422-unit building branded after the Standard Hotel and the 44-stories, 362-unit Lofty Brickell building. The Brickell project marks the first U.S. endeavor for Belgian developer Versluys Group, which was founded in 1908. Prosper, led and founded by former Wall Street financier Jay Roberts, has made inroads in Miami real estate in recent years, though no projects have reached the construction phase yet. Brickell is seeing a rush of luxury development. Along the bayfront, billionaire hedge funder Ken Griffin is planning to build a mixed-use complex, including a 54-story office skyscraper. The Cipriani-branded and St Regis-branded condo projects remain under construction. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Prosper/Versluys acquire Miami Brickell land for $50M, plan $650M 60-story condo tower
1-acre assemblage includes 300+ ft Miami River waterfront; 181 units entitled
Vaster provided $30.5M acquisition loan; $513M construction financing secured last year
stories.summary: A joint venture between Prosper Group and Versluys Group paid $50 million for a 1-acre Brickell waterfront assemblage and plans a 60-story luxury condo tower with 181 units. The property sits near Brickell City Center with significant Miami River frontage. Vaster financed the land acquisition, and the developers previously secured $513 million in construction financing for two condo towers in the same submarket.
stories.impact: Continued capital activity and condo starts in Miami Brickell signal strong investor demand for luxury multifamily and mixed-use in the submarket; waterfront premiums and entitlement velocity (8+ months contract closure) suggest sustained rent growth expectations. For apartment developers, this reinforces Brickell's position as a capital-magnet submarket but may intensify land competition and pricing pressure in South Florida.

stories.title: Hawkins Way, Varde Acquire East Village Student Housing
stories.excerpt: Hawkins Way Capital and joint venture partner Varde Partners completed the acquisition of 81 E. 3rd St., a student housing property located in Manhattan’s East Village. Acquired for $28 million, the off-market transaction marks a strategic addition to the growing FOUND Study student housing portfolio and expands the platform’s presence in one of New York City’s most sought-after neighborhoods. The property features apartment-style layouts that offer an enhanced living experience, compared to traditional dormitory accommodations, according to Hawkins Way. Its flexible design also provides long-term optionality, with the ability to serve both student housing and conventional multifamily uses. “The East Village has long been a market we have targeted, given its concentration of students, proximity to leading universities, and enduring real estate fundamentals,” said Ross Walker, Managing Partner, Hawkins Way. “This acquisition expands our JV’s presence in one of Manhattan’s most dynamic neighborhoods and reinforces our strategy of investing in well-located urban student housing assets positioned to benefit from sustained demand.” The post Hawkins Way, Varde Acquire East Village Student Housing appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Hawkins Way/Varde acquire 81 E. 3rd St. East Village student housing for $28M
Off-market deal expands FOUND Study platform; flexible student-to-multifamily conversion optionality
Asset exhibits apartment-style layouts; positioned for sustained student demand near universities
stories.summary: Hawkins Way Capital and Varde Partners completed an off-market acquisition of 81 E. 3rd St., a student housing property in Manhattan's East Village, for $28 million. The asset features apartment-style living versus dormitory accommodations and offers flexible design enabling conversion to conventional multifamily. The purchase expands the FOUND Study portfolio's presence in a neighborhood with high student concentration and proximity to leading universities.
stories.impact: Student housing investors actively targeting stable, university-proximate East Village stock signals confidence in NYU and adjacent campus enrollment and rental demand; the embedded optionality to convert to market-rate multifamily hedges regulatory/enrollment risk. For apartment developers, this reinforces East Village as a prime micro-market where adaptive use and student-to-young-professional tenant transition pathways underpin valuations and financing feasibility.

stories.title: Former Blue Shield of CA Offices Trade for Residential Conversion
stories.excerpt: NAI Capital Commercial executive managing director Ryan Campbell, SIOR, represented The Olson Company in its $24,850,000 acquisition of a 7.9-acre office campus at 601 Potrero Grande Dr. and 2100 Saturn St. in Monterey Park. The campus includes two office buildings totaling 120,191 square feet. The buyer plans to redevelop the property into a new residential community. Originally built in 1980, the campus was previously owned and occupied by Blue Shield of California. Andrew Harper, Jeff Bramson, and Will Poulsen of JLL represented the seller. “This acquisition reflects the continued shift toward repositioning well-located office properties into much-needed housing throughout the San Gabriel Valley,” said Campbell. “Large infill redevelopment opportunities like this are increasingly rare. The size, location, and long-term potential of this campus make it exceptionally well-suited to deliver new housing while transforming an underutilized office property into a vibrant residential community.” The post Former Blue Shield of CA Offices Trade for Residential Conversion appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Olson Company acquires 120k SF Blue Shield office campus in Monterey Park for $24.85M
7.9-acre site to be redeveloped into residential community; original 1980 build, underutilized
Deal reflects shift toward office-to-residential conversion in San Gabriel Valley
stories.summary: The Olson Company purchased a 7.9-acre, 120,191 square-foot office campus in Monterey Park for $24.85 million, formerly owned and occupied by Blue Shield of California. The buyer plans to redevelop the well-located infill site into a new residential community. The transaction reflects accelerating office-to-housing repositioning across the San Gabriel Valley.
stories.impact: Large infill office-to-multifamily conversions in San Gabriel Valley remain rare and economically viable, signaling continued tight housing supply and strong rental demand in the submarket despite LA's broader office vacancy challenges. For developers, Monterey Park's entitlement and zoning maturity, combined with low acquisition basis relative to new ground-up development, makes office conversion a capital-efficient pathway; monitor zoning/conversion costs but the trade suggests strong rent growth expectations justify repositioning economics.

stories.title: JAMS Relocating New York Offices to 3 Times Square
stories.excerpt: Rudin has secured an agreement with JAMS, a provider of alternative dispute resolution services, to relocate its New York Resolution Center to 3 Times Square. The tenant will occupy 55,335 square feet across the entirety of the building’s top two floors. As part of the 11-year lease, JAMS is expected to move from its current offices at 620 Eighth Ave. in the fourth quarter of 2027. “JAMS’ major commitment to 3 Times Square underscores the market’s continued appetite for top-quality, well-located properties with premier amenity programs,” said Michael Rudin, co-CEO of Rudin. “JAMS joins a diverse roster of high-caliber companies who value vibrant, transit-connected Midtown Manhattan office destinations.” Rudin was represented in-house by Kevin Daly along with the Cushman & Wakefield team of Ron LoRusso, Lou D’Avanzo, John Cefaly, Michael Burgio, Dan Organ and Paige Engeldrum. Ken Rapp, Brendan Herlihy and Ron Wade of CBRE represented JAMS. The post JAMS Relocating New York Offices to 3 Times Square appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JAMS relocates NYC Resolution Center to 3 Times Square; 55,335 SF, 11-year lease
Move from 620 Eighth Ave. occurs Q4 2027; occupies building's top two floors
Rudin cites strong market appetite for transit-connected Midtown Manhattan office space
stories.summary: Rudin secured an 11-year lease with JAMS (alternative dispute resolution services) for 55,335 square feet across the top two floors of 3 Times Square. JAMS will relocate from 620 Eighth Ave. in Q4 2027. Rudin highlighted the tenant's major commitment as evidence of sustained demand for premier, transit-connected Midtown office properties.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. Office leasing momentum in Midtown does not directly signal apartment demand; however, if JAMS' move reflects broader professional services concentration in Times Square, sustained office employment could underpin residential absorption in adjacent Midtown/Hell's Kitchen neighborhoods. Monitor office-to-apartment conversion arbitrage in the area, but this deal alone is office-focused.

stories.title: Shopoff Sells Site of Proposed Newport Beach Condo Development
stories.excerpt: Shopoff Realty Investments has sold a proposed 1.06-acre condominium development, Park Palm in Newport Beach, to Shea Homes for an undisclosed sum. The property is part of Shopoff’s master plan community, Uptown Newport Village, and is entitled for 23 townhomes. Shopoff acquired the 25-acre Uptown Newport Village site in December 2010. The firm set out to repurpose the land for a mixed-use residential village, rather than maintain its prior office and industrial uses. In 2013, Shopoff completed the entitlement process, allowing for master development to include 1,244 residential units, 11,500 square feet of commercial/retail space and two one-acre parks. Phase I of the project has seen multiple developments completed, beginning with One Uptown Newport in 2019. Park Palm, which has been entitled for 23 townhomes, will round out Phase I. Construction on Park Palm is anticipated to begin in 2027, with completion expected in 2028-2029. The post Shopoff Sells Site of Proposed Newport Beach Condo Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Shopoff sells Park Palm site in Newport Beach to Shea Homes; 23-unit townhome development
1.06-acre parcel part of larger Uptown Newport Village 1,244-unit master plan
Construction start planned 2027; completion expected 2028-2029
stories.summary: Shopoff Realty Investments sold Park Palm, a 1.06-acre, 23-townhome site in Newport Beach, to Shea Homes. The property is part of the larger Uptown Newport Village master plan (1,244 residential units, 11,500 SF retail, two parks). Phase I developments have been completed since 2019; Park Palm will round out Phase I with construction beginning in 2027.
stories.impact: Portfolio sales of parcels within entitled master-plan communities, especially to regional builders like Shea Homes, indicate Shopoff's strategic shift to monetize entitled but non-core assets and reflect confidence in Orange County's long-cycle multifamily fundamentals. For developers, Uptown Newport's multi-year phasing cadence and sustained entitlement success (since 2013) confirm OC's supply constraints and developer patience for absorption; monitor Shea's pricing and lease-up velocity in 2028–2029 for Orange County rent growth signals.

stories.title: JLL Lists Staten Island Waterfront Development for $45M
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets has been retained by Traingle Equities as sales advisor for Lighthouse Point, a newly completed, transit-oriented, Class A multifamily waterfront development located at 5 Bay St. in the St. George neighborhood of Staten Island. The asking price is $45 million. Lighthouse Point is a mixed-use development situated adjacent to the Staten Island Ferry Terminal. Occupying the site of the historic U.S. Lighthouse Service’s General Depot, the recently completed first phase features 115 residential units. The JLL Capital Markets Investment Sales and Advisory team representing the seller is led by Senior Managing Directors Rob Hinckley and Jeff Julien, Managing Director Steven Rutman and Director Devon Warren. “Lighthouse Point presents a rare opportunity in today’s market,” said Warren. “It’s a well-conceived project in a market where new development opportunities are increasingly limited, and we think buyers will recognize both the quality of what’s been built and the potential that’s still ahead.” The post JLL Lists Staten Island Waterfront Development for $45M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Triangle Equities lists Lighthouse Point (Staten Island Ferry-adjacent) for $45M; 115 units, recently completed
Class A mixed-use waterfront, transit-oriented; new phase one from historic lighthouse depot site
JLL Capital Markets retained; rare new-supply opportunity in limited Staten Island development market
stories.summary: Triangle Equities, via JLL Capital Markets, is marketing Lighthouse Point, a newly completed, 115-unit Class A multifamily waterfront development in Staten Island's St. George neighborhood adjacent to the Staten Island Ferry Terminal. The mixed-use project occupies the former U.S. Lighthouse Service General Depot site. Asking price is $45 million with significant future development potential.
stories.impact: New supply in transit-oriented Staten Island—a historically underserved multifamily market—combined with ferry adjacency and historic redevelopment positioning signals investor confidence in outer-NYC demand and property quality. For apartment developers, Lighthouse Point's successful delivery and strong asking basis ($391k per unit) in a limited-supply submarket validate ferry-adjacent, transit-oriented development feasibility; Staten Island's zoning constraints and underinvestment create a runway for forward-looking acquisitions and conversions ahead of rising commute-flexibility demand.

stories.title: Brookfield Asset Management Raises Record $77B in Q2

The firm also secured $5 billion in commitments for its first AI Infrastructure Fund. bullets: Brookfield Asset Management raises record $77B in Q2 2026; AUM exceeds $1 trillion
Year-to-date raised $98B; deployed $21B last quarter; flagship PE fund at $6.7B, infrastructure at $9.3B
$5B committed to first AI Infrastructure Fund; $25B Bloom Energy AI power financing framework
stories.summary: Brookfield Asset Management reported a record $77 billion in capital raised during Q2 2026, bringing total assets under management above $1 trillion. Year-to-date raises of $98 billion exceed half of 2025's annual total. The firm deployed $21 billion in the quarter and is channeling significant capital into AI infrastructure and power, including a $5 billion AI Infrastructure Fund and a $25 billion financing framework with Bloom Energy.
stories.impact: Record capital formation at mega-scale asset manager signals robust institutional appetite for alternative assets, infrastructure, and AI-adjacent investments; however, multifamily implications depend on Brookfield's deployment priorities. If institutional capital rotates toward AI data-center adjacent real estate or power infrastructure over traditional apartment development, it may tighten multifamily construction capital availability and cap rates. Monitor Brookfield's multifamily portfolio activity and any strategic announcements on residential exposure.

stories.title: Return-to-Office Gained New Momentum in First Half of 2026: Report
stories.excerpt: U.S. office attendance is on the rise, but the return-to-office trend remains a tale of two cities. In the first half of 2026, office visits nationwide rose 6 percent year-over-year, and achieved the narrowest first-half gap from pre-pandemic levels thus far, data from foot-traffic tracker Placer.ai shows. The six-month period of foot traffic marked acceleration from the 1.9 percent annual uptick observed in the same period of 2025. Office attendance is far from a full and even recovery, however. U.S. office visits remain 31.2 percent below 2019 levels, according to Placer.ai’s August office market report. While Miami and New York are making strides toward baseline visitation levels, Denver and Chicago still have a long way to go. The hybrid workweek also appears here to stay –– for now. The report’s survey of 11 major U.S. markets revealed that office attendance diverges widely across geographies. Cubicles and corner offices are filling up in Miami, where attendance in the first half of the year was 11.5 percent below that of 2019. First-half attendance in Denver, on the other hand, remained more than 40 percent below 2019 levels. The “most improved” award for the period of January through June goes to West Coast hubs Los Angeles and San Francisco, with annual visitation upticks of 13 percent and 10.9 percent, respectively. The pair of cities achieved the report’s largest year-over-year gains. Hybrid workweeks have made a lasting impact on U.S. corporate culture, but the model’s popularity is waning in some markets. The country’s highest shares of Friday office attendance belong to Miami and Dallas, where roughly one in seven weekday office visits fell on a Friday. In Chicago, however, Fridays account for less than one out of every 10 office visits. This is the same city where personalized video platform Cameo announced last year a $10,000 raise for every new and existing employee that returns to its Fulton Market office four days per week. Miami and New York are approaching baseline recovery, while Denver and Chicago lag with visits more than 40 percent below 2019. Hybrid work continues to persist across major markets.
stories.impact: Divergent office recovery by metro creates mixed signals for apartment demand: Miami and NYC's stronger office return-to-office momentum may support downtown/CBD-proximate rental demand and justify transit-oriented residential development; Denver and Chicago's persistent weakness could dampen employment growth and apartment absorption in those markets, making apartment development riskier without demographic or population migration tailwinds. For developers, office recovery geography should inform site selection and timing; prioritize Miami/NYC infill conversions and CBD-adjacent projects over Denver/Chicago greenfiled unless powered by population inflow or alternative employment clusters.

stories.title: Krea USA Nabs $62M Construction Loan for Lauderhill, Fla., Rental
stories.excerpt: Krea USA nabbed a $61.8 million construction loan for a multifamily development in Lauderhill, Fla., property records show. The financing from Abanca Bank covers the 385-unit Le Parc at Lauderhill development, at 3831 Northwest 13th Street, just east of the Lauderhill Mall and North State Road 7. The 10-acre development will include three eight-story buildings, including a day care operated by a nonprofit and no other commercial space on the ground floor. Construction started in March and is expected to be completed next year. The project has undergone a few changes since first being pitched in 2020. It was originally envisioned as a workforce housing development, with Vivian Dimond’s Bayshore Capital Grove as a partner. Fast forward six years, the development will have no rental restrictions, and Krea USA bought out Bayshore Capital Grove’s stake, Akrisht Pandey, Krea USA’s director of real estate, told Commercial Observer. Still, a tax abatement amounting to $9.1 million over 10 years, which the City of Lauderhill approved in 2022, will remain, Pandey added. Rents are expected to range between 100 and 120 percent of the area’s median income. The developer will build a public road. Krea USA, led by founder and CEO Mauricio Girault, specializes in mixed-income multifamily residential properties. In January, the Miami-based firm proposed building an affordable homeownership condominium in Miami’s Overtown neighborhood on land owned by the city, the South Florida Business Journal reported. A representative for Bayshore Capital Grove did not respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Krea USA secures $61.8M construction loan from Abanca Bank for 385-unit Lauderhill rental
Le Parc at Lauderhill: 10-acre, three 8-story buildings; construction started March, completion 2027
No rental restrictions; Krea bought out workforce-housing co-developer; $9.1M tax abatement (10-year)
stories.summary: Krea USA obtained a $61.8 million construction loan from Abanca Bank for Le Parc at Lauderhill, a 385-unit, 10-acre multifamily development in Lauderhill, Florida. The project includes three 8-story buildings and a nonprofit day care; construction began in March with completion expected in 2027. Originally envisioned as workforce housing, the development now carries no rental restrictions. Krea bought out co-developer Bayshore Capital Grove; a $9.1 million municipal tax abatement over 10 years remains in place.
stories.impact: South Florida construction financing remains available and active; Lauderhill's tax abatement and suburban infill positioning reflect municipality efforts to densify. Krea's shift from workforce to market-rate signals strong rent growth expectations in the Lauderhill corridor post-completion (2027); continued tax incentives and construction loan availability in South Florida support pipeline momentum. For developers, monitor Lauderhill/Broward multifamily deliveries and lease-up velocity—if Krea achieves strong rents without restrictions, it validates market-rate feasibility and may trigger additional supply competition.

stories.title: In Largest U.S. Multifamily Sale Since 2024, BlackRock Pays $1.63B in SoCal
stories.excerpt: BlackRock has acquired more than 3,600 rental residential units in Southern California in one of the region’s largest commercial real estate deals in recent memory. It’s also the largest U.S. multifamily sale since June 2024. One of the investment vehicles run by the asset management titan put down $1.63 billion for Camden Property Trust’s 11-property portfolio. The portfolio is 96 percent occupied, with 3,620 apartment units in Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside and San Diego counties. JLL Capital Markets announced the deal Wednesday after it represented Houston-based Camden in the sale, and arranged $566.6 million in agency acquisition financing for the buyer. The financing covers seven of the properties and consists of a five-year, fixed-rate, interest-only loan structured to allow each asset to be sold or refinanced independently. JLL said the deal is one of the biggest apartment portfolio deals ever completed in Southern California, and that the assets represent roughly 16.5 percent of the region’s average annual multifamily transaction volume by unit count over the past five years. The portfolio includes the Camden, a 287-unit Hollywood development with nearly 39,000 square feet of retail anchored by an Equinox gym; the 380-unit Camden Crown Valley in Mission Viejo; the 469-unit Camden Landmark in Ontario, representing roughly 5 percent of that city’s institutional apartment inventory; and the 132-unit Camden Hillcrest in San Diego, where JLL said no multifamily property with more than 100 units has traded in the past decade. “The significant investor demand for these best-in-class assets in supply-constrained markets underscores the strength of Southern California fundamentals, leading to significant liquidity at scale,” Blake Rogers, senior managing director and multifamily platform leader at JLL, said in a statement. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BlackRock acquires Camden Property Trust 11-property portfolio for $1.63B; 3,620 units across Southern California
96% occupied; covers LA, Orange, Riverside, San Diego counties; largest multifamily sale since June 2024
JLL arranged $566.6M agency acquisition financing; five-year fixed-rate, interest-only, independent asset sale structure
stories.summary: BlackRock acquired Camden Property Trust's 11-property portfolio comprising 3,620 rental units across Southern California counties for $1.63 billion. The portfolio is 96 percent occupied and represents roughly 16.5 percent of regional supply. JLL Capital Markets represented Camden and arranged $566.6 million in agency acquisition financing structured as a five-year fixed-rate, interest-only loan with independent asset sale optionality. This is the largest U.S. multifamily sale since June 2024.
stories.impact: Mega-cap institutional buyer (BlackRock) acquiring stabilized, fully-leased regional portfolios at scale signals strong confidence in Southern California multifamily fundamentals, rent growth, and capital stability despite macro uncertainty. The deal's financing structure (five-year fixed, interest-only with asset-level sale optionality) and 96% occupancy reflect investor focus on cash-flow yield and flexibility. For apartment developers, BlackRock's entry reinforces SoCal as a core hold market and may increase cap-rate compression; however, the portfolio's maturity (existing stock) vs. new development suggests limited direct development impact unless it signals institutional appetite for new-supply acquisitions post-stabilization.
